question: Which exact completion effects constrain surviving guest APIs when draw, replay, present and ring bodies are replaced together, and where does the evidence within the inspected scope stop?

scope.boundary: Static contract and explicit open questions, not every device or resource alias, complete queue reclamation, runtime equivalence or a safe renderer cut. A separate exact-function finding had at most eight direct functions; generated semantic reads had at most 200 lines per window.
scope.candidateHybrid: Keep guest setters, getters, creators and dispatch tables; replace all draw entries, scratch begin and commit, Clear, Resolve, tiling and replay, predication, present and ring entries together. Internal fields need preservation only when a surviving reader or callback still observes them.
scope.continuationFunctions: Device initialization 0x8268D220/0x8268D278/0x8268D2C8/0x826A6380/0x826A63E8 and fill 0x827F7BB0; submit and list 0x8269BD98/0x826AC218/0x826AC020/0x826AC3F8/0x826ABB90/0x826ABA68; exact allocation and callback findings.

dependencies.use: Surviving API, object, dispatch-table and outside busy and wait clients.
Accepted per-body API roles and partial classification of which code holds, replaces and releases the data.
Resource wait callers and the distinct lock-selected resource+0xC fence.
Separate command storage, primary-ring publication and unclosed exact link for the span that code holds, replaces and releases.
List-selected replay writes without the code that holds, replaces and releases the allocation, or the full set of outside readers.
Accepted presentation callback, selector and fence dependencies.

fenceArithmetic.label: V
fenceArithmetic.notation: G=*(*0x820009F0); B=load32(G+0x2A90); P=load32(G+0x2A9C); C=load32(B+0); U(x)=x modulo2^32; f is a requested scalar fence.
fenceArithmetic.busy: 0x8269C6C0 returned 0 for f=0. If f=P it called 0x8269C588 before reloading P and C. It returned 1 exactly when U(P-f)<U(P-C), comparing unsigned 32 values; otherwise 0. Wrapper 0x8269C738 loaded f from resource+8. This was not a signed half-range comparison.
fenceArithmetic.wait: 0x8269BE70 exited for f=0 or U(P-f)>=U(P-C). While pending, r7 low byte 0 and f=P selected an early exit for G+0x33B0!=0 or a C588 flush otherwise. It rechecked the predicate and bracketed polling with 0x8268CAA8/0x8268CAD8. Poll 0x8268CBB8 could escape independently; residual r3 was not established as a canonical HRESULT.
fenceArithmetic.emitter: 0x8269BCA8 emitted INVALIDATE_STATE then two C0025800 EVENT_WRITE_SHD packets with initiator 3: encoded physical(B+4)|2 received G+0x30|(G+0x3A48&3), then encoded physical(B)|2 received oldP. It stored U(oldP+2) to G+0x2A9C at 0x8269BD84.
fenceArithmetic.guardedCpuWrites: Only when G+0x541C==0 and byte G+0x2ABD&2 did BCA8 also directly write B+0=oldP followed by B+4=cursor before advancing P. The branch at 0x8269BD60 skipped these stores for a nonzero 541C. This guarded CPU order differed from GPU packet order and was not ordinary GPU-retirement proof.
fenceArithmetic.initialization: 0x8269C8E0 allocated and zeroed 96-byte B and separate 32-byte S2 at G+0x2A94. It selected P=3 only for oldP=0, otherwise retainedP; set C=U(P-2), B+4=cursor and G+0x2AC8=0. B+0x3C was separately registered with VdEnableRingBufferRPtrWriteBack; B+8 with VdSetSystemCommandBufferGpuIdentifierAddress.
fenceArithmetic.qualification: The modular rule is exact for these readers. Reset epochs, outstanding distance and aliases remain inputs. Ring RPTR, next issue ticket and completed ticket are distinct.

zeroPReachability.label: I
zeroPReachability.knownTransitions: After successful C8E0 on a fresh zero-filled device, P=3. C8E0 preserves an old nonzero P; BCA8 adds 2 modulo 2^32. Reset 0x8268CE90 calls C8E0 and has no own P store. Captured suspend 0x8268CF60/resume 0x8268CFF8 bodies have no own P store. Odd parity survives these identified paths and wrap, so none reaches P=0.
zeroPReachability.preInit: Before first ring success the known state is P=0 and 2AA0=0. The known binder and resource zero-P mask test 0&resource[0] is false. No direct pre-init binder appears in D2C8/D278/A6380/A63E8. C8E0 failure can leave the freshly published device at P=0; its externally usable lifetime and later writers are unclosed.
zeroPReachability.stop: This is a known-transition invariant, not global P==0 unreachability. Indirect callbacks, imported effects, indexed, rebased, overlapping, atomic and copy writers and the unclassified 0x8319AEA8 candidate remain uncovered. No pre-init record decoder or complete binder reachability was established.

resourceRecords.record: Observed appenders wrote an 8-byte value: pointer-derived first word, second word 0xFFFFFFFF, then cursor+=8. Binders cleared bit 30; result-reader and Resolve producers set bit 30. The record decoder and exact class meaning were not identified. No observed append itself decremented resource+4, called Release or freed a resource.
resourceRecords.adjacentQueue: 0x826A6A08 requested 34 dwords=136 bytes, alignment 128; separateG+0x34DC/34E0/34E4 described a16-record payload after an 8-byte header. It was not the 34D4 drain. 0x826A72F8 flushed cache lines and synchronized; it did not clear the payload.
resourceRecords.release: 0x826981D8 atomically decremented resource+4; zero could recursively release a type 4 child then call 0x82697AA8. That cleanup selected type-specific resource+8 waits through BE70 before physical frees through 0x82E29160 on captured paths. It did not directly consume G+0x34D4.
resourceRecords.drainFrontier: The queue was a deferred resource-record and stamp candidate, not a proved pending-release list. Its initial mask and cursors are zero, and known successful ticket transitions stay odd. A nonzero mask writer and a P=0 reachable producer would be required to activate the known append guard. Global unreachability, an exact decoder, drain trigger and segment reclamation are not yet established. Advancing P and C alone is not equivalent processing if such a surviving path is reached.

C810 separately spins on N after its fence wait.
submissionAndCallbacks.ringIndex: 0x8269B900 used G+0x2AC8, primary base G+0x3A30 and mask G+0x3A34 for masked command writes; it published the index at 0x8269BA84 and MMIO 0x7FC80714 at 0x8269BA90 with sync and eieio. Optional G+0x541C/G+0x5B0C sinks were separate indirect boundaries. Index and RPTR progression did not itself write C.
submissionAndCallbacks.registration: 0x826A62F8 called VdSetGraphicsInterruptCallback at 0x826A6364, continuation 0x826A6368, with r3=0x8269B450,r4=G. The guest handler received event selector r3 and G in r4.
submissionAndCallbacks.handler: For event 1, 0x8269B450 loaded callback=S2+0x10, trapped after a debug call for 0x0BADF00D, and otherwise called a nonzero callback with r3=load32(S2+0x14). Under G+0x2A98 lock it cleared the current CPU bit from S2+0 and masked to 0x3F. For event 0, MMIO 0x7FC86544 bit 0 was the requirement for 0x826A3EB8.
submissionAndCallbacks.presentCallbacks: 0x826A3EB8/0x826A3FB8 updated a distinct G+0x413C/4140 queue, counters and timing and S2+4 or MMIO 0x7FC86110. A3EB8 used optional callback G+0x40A0; A3FB8 used G+0x409C. These bodies did not directly store G+0x2B00; transitive or aliased writers remained unknown. 0x8269BF40 emitted callback, interrupt and wait commands; command construction was not callback execution.
submissionAndCallbacks.qualification: S2 denoted the block at G+0x2A94. EVENT_WRITE stores, RPTR writeback, callback acknowledgements, vblank queue state and guarded CPU recovery were separate producers. No single observed word replaced their whole protocol.
submissionAndCallbacks.rootQueueJoin: AC218 finalizes L=G+0x3438 through B508 at 0x826AC2B8. For nonnull L+4, B508 writes an encoded tail link and exact C0000000 at [L+8] at 0x8269B53C. AC218 emits AC020 with the encoded L[0] root or zero at 0x826AC32C and its counted middle BD98 r7=1 at 0x826AC3B0 unless the captured guarded bypass applies. Whether the middle descriptor is direct or deferred, AC020 is the original root callback; the direct two-word submit descriptor need not carry that root terminator.
submissionAndCallbacks.queueIdentity: AC3F8's selected constructor stores W=G+0x2AC0 and CPU ordinali at Q_i+0/+4, Q_i=G+0x2C3C+80*i. AC020 places incoming r3 in Q_cpu+0x40+4*(producer&3), increments Q_cpu+0x38 and signals Q_cpu+0x20. BB90 pops a queue item, increments W+0x3C at 0x826ABC58 and advances Q_i+0x3C at 0x826ABC74. Those are worker participation, distinct from N.
submissionAndCallbacks.normalRetirement: ABB90 passes exact C000 to ABA68 at 0x826ABDD4; nonexact C-class links continue at link+4. UnderW+0x44, ABA68 clears the current CPU participation bit and decrements W+0x3C at 0x826ABACC. On its final 0 transition, it advances selected CPU queue consumers, and decrements W+0x40=N at 0x826ABB34 only if W+0x48 is null. The six-CPU cleanup does not decrement N per CPU. This reconciles the normal writer recorded in RVA-F-0303; watchdog A5B48 zero remains separate.
submissionAndCallbacks.pendingContinuation: AB740's 0x88 arm can retain an advanced cursor in W+0x48 and switch to W+0x54. After popping an item, BB90's first participant selects and clears a nonnull W48; otherwise it selects the fresh queued root+4 and saves that root at W4C. Later participants resume W24. A pending cursor suppresses retirement at the earlier final active transition; only a final transition with no pending cursor decrements N.
submissionAndCallbacks.conservationLimit: I: ordered normal-path event accounting is N_end=U(N_start+sum(selected BD98 r7)-D), where D counts ABA68 exact-C000 final active transitions with null W48. The counted middle submit and root callback are structurally linked. A global equality D=sum(r7), exactly-once delivery for every valid root or pending chain, indirect submit or callback aliases, empty or failure roots and imported synchronization or runtime progress are not proved. The decrement applies only under a condition, per completed aggregate root and continuation group, not per BD98 descriptor, nested link or CPU.

scratchPair.inspectedCallers: 0x8250E718 and 0x82512608 supplied count 4, stride 20, giving q=20 dwords=80 bytes. Their stores covered returned pointer+0 through+76 as four 20-byte vertices; the first five words were not the whole buffer. Requested alignment was 16.
scratchPair.endVertices: 0x826A2FF0 loaded one word from G+0x3484 and stored it to G+0x30, then returned. It did not copy a 20-byte vertex buffer or read all vertex bytes on the CPU. The emitted GPU fetch described the upload; whether the backing is preserved or reused after commit was not closed.
scratchPair.allocatorBoundary: 0x8269B818 selected 0x8269B618, 0x826A6848 or an indirect manager route through 0x826A6AB8; no specific system allocation or code that holds, replaces and releases the 6 MB extent was linked. Separately 0x8269C170 passed 4224 dwords and alignment 128 to B818, staging 16896 requested bytes, but linked a [H+4,H+4220) record area and flushed through H+4224. Those units and extents were distinct.
scratchPair.qualification: BeginVertices and EndVertices remained candidate names for the exact scratch-producing and commit behavior. Preserve writable 80 bytes through the paired commit for these observed calls; other count and stride forms, failure semantics and post-commit lifetime need their own caller link. The reported 6 MB allocation was not proved to back this upload or all list records.

candidateContract.label: I
obligations: Retain valid G, resource headers and scalar stamps while surviving API, Release and wait clients read them. Issue the captured logical ticket with U(P+2), publish its completed C only after equivalent prior host work retires, and preserve the exact unsigned predicate across wrap and reset epochs.

For a surviving counted submission, retire N separately from completed C. Replace the root callback, per-CPU queue participation and pending continuation as one coherent effect; a root group retires only after its active participation reaches 0 with no pending W48. r7=0 descriptor calls add no independent unit. Model applicable S2 acknowledgement, RPTR and ring-space progression when their consumers survive. C810 requires its separate N loop to reach 0.

Initial mask 0 suppresses the known P=0 append guard; known successful ticket paths stay odd. Remove 34D4 only after closing failed-init exposure, hidden P and mask writers and surviving producers and consumers, or preserve the actual decoder, drain and reclamation. Do not invent Release calls or clear unknown records.
Return writable aligned scratch for surviving scratch callers and consume their upload before reuse. The known count 4, stride 20 form needs 80 bytes at requestedalignment 16, not 20 bytes.

Bridge callback and present state only for surviving consumers. AC020 queueing, A3FB8 present effects and A8BE8's optional sink are real or unresolved effects; optional G347C/G409C/G40A0 installers and lifetimes remain unbound. Drop their protocols only with their producers, effects and consumers together. A returned VdSwap, readable frontbuffer, RPTR or watchdog escape does not prove host and GPU completion.
candidateContract.sufficiency: These are necessary obligations that apply only under their stated conditions. Normal decrement and initial zero fill are closed, but global group conservation, aliases, deferred-record reachability and decoder and physical backing lifetime prevent a complete implementable hybrid contract.
